observation.visible_scene: A tight close-up of a window screen or wire mesh (fine vertical wires visible) covered with condensation droplets and streaky wet patches. A bright yellow-green fuzzy textile (chenille/microfiber-like) occupies the right edge, partly overlapping a pale vertical frame bar. Behind/beside that bar on the far right is a dark object showing curved tan/yellow segments. The screen fills the left and center of the frame throughout.
visible_changes: The framing drifts slowly across the clip: the wet-screen pattern changes in scale and density (vertical wires look finer/denser on the left by the end), indicating a gradual camera pan/zoom rather than the screen itself altering.
The yellow fuzzy textile moves toward the bottom-right corner of the frame, occupying less of the right side over time.
More of the dark tan-curved object on the right becomes visible from top to bottom as the clip progresses.
The pale vertical frame bar shifts slightly rightward, with minor wobble between frames.
The droplet/frost patches on the screen remain essentially static between consecutive frames; no dripping or wiping motion of the screen surface is clearly visible.
No independent motion of the screen or of the dark object is confirmed; their apparent positional changes are consistent with the camera reframing.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the yellow textile is held by an unseen hand and is being used to wipe or is simply resting out of frame.
What the dark tan-curved object actually is (its full shape lies outside the crop).
Whether this segment is part of a cleaning/wiping action or a passive observation, since both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
Any motion before t=0 or after the last frame.
uncertain_details: The split between camera movement and object movement is not fully resolvable: the yellow textile's apparent downward drift could be camera tilt/pan or the textile being moved, and no hand is visible to decide.
Exact identity/material of the screen (mesh vs ribbed glass) and of the right-side objects is not certain from the frames alone.
The small frame-to-frame jitter of the white bar suggests handheld camera motion but is not definitive.
